rulings.raw: 1 8oz box of frilly protein pasta (like Loppdy Loops or Campanelle, use gluten free as needed)
rulings.evidence: Legume-fortified pasta (Barilla Protein+, Banza and the like) is its own SKU at roughly 0.19-0.25 per oz against the board's commodity semolina pasta at 0.057 per oz - a real price class, and the recipe's whole protein claim rests on it, so I will not bridge it onto [pasta]. Shape (frilly/campanelle) is not a pricing question.

No commodity claims it and captures carry matching products. Refused the chicken-broth bridge: bone broth is a 6-8 dollar quart against a 1.50-2.50 broth carton and carries 10 g protein per cup against about 1 - different product, different price class, different macros.

The line itself allows store-bought, and pesto is a live board id at 6 of 7 - the same call as the 2026-08-26 'Homemade Barbecue Sauce' -> bbq-sauce ruling. Macros taken from a jarred basil pesto label, which is what a shopper buying to this line actually gets.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Searched by food, not string: the board's only pasta ids are the generic [pasta] (7/7, 0.057/oz at Sam's, semolina) and [rotini-pasta], both commodity dry pasta; nothing in commodities, recipe-commodities, the everyday board or the feed prices a legume-fortified protein pasta under any spelling (checked chickpea/lentil/banza/protein wordings). Barilla Protein+ and Banza run 3-4x the per-ounce price of commodity pasta and carry 10-14 g protein per 2 oz against 7, so pricing this line at [pasta] would publish a materially wrong cost on the line the recipe is named for.

No commodity claims it in any namespace; the near ids are chicken-broth and beef-broth, both boxed stock at roughly 1.50-2.50 per 32 oz, while bone broth (Kettle & Fire, Swanson Sipping Bone Broth) is 5-8 dollars for the same carton and is a different food on the label - 10 g protein per cup against about 1. The 2026-08-26 'reduced sodium beef broth' -> beef-broth precedent does not reach this: that was the same carton with a label variant, this is a different SKU at a different price class.
